newsitem.title: USA: IRIDIUM satellite launch reset for January 11.
newsitem.headline: IRIDIUM satellite launch reset for January 11.

text.p: IRIDIUM LLC said Friday's launch of its first three satellites was rescheduled for Saturday because of a problem with the initiation of the water suppression system.
The system is used to protect the launch pad and dampen the acoustics encountered during liftoff.

The launch was postponed Wednesday and Thursday because of technical problems. Motorola Inc has about a 25 percent stake in IRIDIUM, a consortium that is working to provide a global communications network using 66 low-orbit satellites.
IRIDIUM is an international consortium of 17 companies and organizations, including Motorola, Sprint Corp, Lockheed Martin Corp, Pacific Electric Wire & Cable Co and Raytheon Co.
The three satellites are to be carried into orbit by a McDonnell Douglas Corp Delta II rocket from Vandenberg Air Force Base in Lompoc, Calif.
